questions.text: A building straddling two fire zones has exactly 400 sq m in the Highly Fire Restrictive Zone out of a total of 1,200 sq m. Which zone governs the entire building under PD 1096 Rule V, Sec. 502?

options.text: Highly Fire Restrictive Zone, because 400 sq m is the larger portion of the building, thus requiring stricter compliance
Highly Fire Restrictive Zone, because 400 sq m is more than one-third of 1,200 sq m, triggering the need for enhanced fire safety measures
Less restrictive zone, because exactly one-third (400/1,200) means the triggering condition ('more than one-third') is not met
Building Official discretion determines which zone applies, allowing for case-by-case assessment based on specific building conditions

questions.rationale: This is the 'exactly one-third' trap. The Code says 'more than one-third' — at exactly 1/3, the less restrictive zone governs. Exam questions specifically present 400/1,200 to test this nuance.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule V, Sec. 503, what are the fire zone compliance requirements for a pre-engineered building that is dismantled and relocated to a different fire zone?

options.text: The building may retain its original fire zone compliance certification if it was legally compliant at the previous location and no structural changes are made
The building must comply with all requirements for buildings in the new fire zone, regardless of its previous compliance status
The building is exempt from fire zone requirements if it was manufactured to any recognized standard and has not been altered
Relocation is not covered under Sec. 503; general building permit requirements apply instead, necessitating a new compliance review

questions.rationale: This prevents a common loophole: PEBs designed for rural/agricultural sites (Non-Fire Restricted Zone) being moved to industrial zones (Fire Restrictive or Highly Fire Restrictive) without upgrades.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule V, Sec. 506(e), after a typhoon damages a non-conforming building in a Fire Restrictive Zone, what is the cost cap and material requirement for repair?

options.text: ≤20% of appraised value; same or better materials allowed
≤20% of replacement cost; same kind of materials as original construction
≤20% of building value; any non-combustible material permitted
≤20% of replacement cost; any material permitted as long as Building Official approves

questions.rationale: Pathway C uses 'value of the existing building' (appraised/market value). Pathway E uses 'replacement cost' (higher). This distinction is frequently tested. Replacement cost > appraised value, so the same absolute peso amount may be compliant under E but not under C.

questions.text: Using the 'NRH — No Rush Here' mnemonic under PD 1096 Rule V, what do the letters stand for in ascending order of fire zone restriction?

N = Non-Fire Restricted Zone (Types I, II; no fire resistivity), R = Fire Restrictive Zone (Types II, III, IV; 2 hr exterior / 1 hr interior), H = Highly Fire Restrictive Zone (Types IV, V; 3–4 hr throughout)
N = Not fire-rated, R = Rated, H = Highly rated — each zone requires progressively more fire testing and certification
N = National zoning, R = Regional, H = Highly local — increasing administrative jurisdiction with specific local ordinances

A special permit from the Building Official is required for a limited period; the structure must be completely removed upon permit expiration

The structure must conform to IBC temporary structure standards for a certificate to be issued, aligning with international guidelines

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule V, Sec. 505, what measuring convention applies when determining fire separation distance for buildings adjacent to a street or alley?

options.text: The edge of the sidewalk is used as the property line for distance measurement, which is a common misinterpretation.
The center line of the adjoining street or alley may be considered an adjacent property line; distances measured at right angles to the street
The face of the building on the opposite side of the street is used as the reference point, which is incorrect.
Distance is measured from the property line to the face of the building, regardless of street width, which is a frequent error.

questions.rationale: This convention is consistent with Rule VII, Sec. 704-705. The full half-width of the street corridor counts as effective fire separation distance, relaxing exterior wall fire resistance requirements for buildings on wide streets.

Total demolition; relocation; 20% repair/alteration (Pathway C); fire wall-separated addition (Pathway D); fortuitous event repair (Pathway E)
Full code upgrade; partial demolition; sprinkler installation in lieu of compliance; temporary permit renewal, which are not all recognized pathways
Grandfathering for historic buildings; 20% repair/alteration; fortuitous event repair, which does not cover all possible pathways

questions.rationale: Each pathway is an independent option — the owner picks one. The pathways are mutually exclusive for any given scope of work. Pathway C and E both use a 20% threshold but with different denominators and different triggers.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule V, Sec. 501, what is the definition and purpose of fire zones?

options.text: Areas where only certain building materials are prohibited based on their combustibility, ensuring compliance with local fire safety regulations

Areas within which only certain types of buildings are permitted based on their use, type of construction, and resistance to fire — for the management, prevention, control, and suppression of conflagration
Areas designated by the Bureau of Fire Protection for mandatory sprinkler installation, regardless of building height or occupancy type
Areas where the Building Official has authority to override all construction type requirements, provided that the overall fire safety is not compromised

questions.rationale: The word 'conflagration' in Sec. 507 is deliberate and testable — it distinguishes urban-scale fire spread from individual building fires. Fire zones exist to break the chain of fire spreading from building to building across an urban block.

questions.text: Pathway E under Sec. 506 permits repairs to a fire-damaged nonconforming building using the same construction materials. What is the cost threshold that governs this pathway?

options.text: Repairs may use original materials if cost does not exceed 10% of the building's replacement cost
Repairs may use original materials if cost does not exceed 20% of the building's replacement cost
Repairs may use original materials if cost does not exceed 30% of the building's replacement cost
Repairs may use original materials regardless of cost if the building retains its original occupancy

questions.text: Under PD 1096, how many fire zone classifications does the National Building Code establish for the Philippines?

options.text: Two fire zone types: restricted and unrestricted
Three fire zone types with progressively stricter requirements
Four fire zone types mirroring international building code conventions
Five fire zone types corresponding to building construction types
